name: TX-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+12 district with incumbent Pat Fallon seeking re-election
Fallon holds about $1 million in cash versus roughly $4,000 for Jason Pearce
Prediction markets price Fallon near 96-97%; no polls or expert ratings exist
No outside spending has been directed against Fallon
model.rationale: A twelve-point Republican lean, an incumbent with a million-dollar war chest, and a challenger who has raised almost nothing leave no visible path to an upset; markets and fundamentals align on a comfortable Fallon win.
model.watch: Only a late external shock, such as adverse news for Fallon or a sudden influx of outside money for Pearce, could move this race toward competitiveness.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 4th District leans Republican by about twelve points, and incumbent Pat Fallon is seeking another term with a substantial financial advantage. He has raised more than $930,000 and holds over $1 million in cash, while Democratic nominee Jason Pearce has raised roughly $26,000 with minimal cash on hand. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Fallon and nothing to oppose him, and no polls or expert ratings track the race.

Prediction markets give Fallon roughly a 96% chance of winning. With the incumbent renominated without difficulty and no visible Democratic infrastructure in the district, the race lacks the ingredients typically associated with an upset. The forecast expects Fallon to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of competitiveness.
